title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: federated Copilot connectors read third-party data live through MCP
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly implies that clearing a publisher type always prevents access, although an individual connector can override that setting. Its blanket claim that blocking has no API also overlooks the documented package-blocking API for connectors distributed as plugin packages. Most licensing, roadmap and connector behaviour claims are supported.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; rendered controls table
claims.claim: Publisher-type availability is managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.

claims.claim: Tenant-wide user access is managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; rendered controls table
claims.claim: Individual connector enablement is located at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your connections.

claims.fix: Complete the path to 'Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > connector > Enable / Disable'; the current path correctly reaches the list holding the control. The cited manage page identifies the actions, and the cited custom-connector setup page documents managing a connector from that list.

claims.where: controls[4].api; Governance controls: no API for these connector settings
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API for blocking individual federated connectors and their tools.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
claims.fix: For connectors distributed as plugin packages, set controls[4].api to kind 'graph', call 'POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackage-block'. Add the note: 'Beta package-level blocking requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence; it blocks the selected package, not individual tools or a shared remote connector used by other packages.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/submit-federated-connector and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers for packaging and scope. Replace the blanket no-API sentence with 'No API is documented for the tenant-wide publisher-type or User access settings, or connector-specific enablement and staging; package-level blocking has a beta Graph API.'
